Well, let me think about this year's crops. I've been at this 20 years, and my 10 mu is all I've got to feed the family.

**Wheat first.** I'll plant around October 10th, same as always, after the maize comes off. I buy seed from the agricultural supply shop in town — the regular wheat variety everyone in the village plants, about 15 yuan per mu worth of seed. I sow a bit thick, maybe 15 kg per mu, because at my age I'd rather have too many seedlings than a thin stand.

For fertilizer, I use what my neighbors use. Before planting I spread two bags of compound fertilizer — that's the 15-15-15 stuff, about 40 kg per mu as base. Then in spring around the jointing time in March, if the wheat looks a bit yellow, I'll topdress urea, maybe 15 kg per mu. That comes out to roughly 14 kg of nitrogen per mu total, which is what I've done for years. Could I use less? My neighbor Old Wang tried cutting back two years ago and his yield dropped, so I don't want to risk it.

Irrigation — the well is there but pumping costs money and electricity isn't cheap. I'll water before winter (the "freeze water" in late November), then once after spring returns, and once at grain filling if there's no rain. Three times total, usually. If it's a wet spring I skip one.

I spray herbicide once in spring for the weeds, and if I see aphids at heading I spray once more. My son comes back from the city to help with harvest in June — we hire a combine driver, costs about 50 yuan per mu.

I expect around 450 kg per mu if the weather is normal. Last year I got 470, year before was 420 because of the dry spring.

**Now maize.** Right after wheat harvest in mid-June, no time to waste — we disc the straw in and plant within a week. I use a hybrid seed, the one the shop recommends, about 30 yuan per mu. My wife and I plant with a small hand planter we share with my brother.

Fertilizer for maize: one bag of compound at planting as base (about 30 kg/mu), then urea topdress at the big trumpet stage, maybe 20 kg/mu. So nitrogen total about 13 kg/mu. Maize takes less fussing than wheat.

Irrigation — summer has more rain, so usually I only need to water once or twice if there's a dry spell at tasseling. I watch the sky.

Herbicide once after planting. Sometimes armyworm shows up and I spray. Harvest end of September, by hand mostly, though if my son helps we hire a small harvester.

Expect 500 kg per mu. That's what I usually get.

Total for the year I figure about 3,500-4,000 yuan in inputs. Not much left after selling, but it's steady. At 70, steady is what I want.
